 Log in Twins Sign Sonny Gray to Two-Year Contract
 27 minutes ago Share share-square--:R1qlq: MINNEAPOLIS-ST. PAUL, MN – The Minnesota Twins announced today that they have agreed to terms on a two-year contract with right-handed pitcher Sonny Gray through the 2028 season.
 Gray, 37, started 29 games for the Boston Red Sox last season, going 18-5 with a 2.72 ERA (169.0 IP, 51 ER), 46 walks, 149 strikeouts, a 1.15 WHIP and a .236 opponent batting average. He led all major league pitchers in wins and led the American League in winning percentage (.783), while finishing fifth in the AL Cy Young Award voting. The former Twin pitched for two seasons in Minnesota from 2022-23, going 16-13 with a 2.90 ERA (303.2 IP, 98 ER), 91 walks, 300 strikeouts, a 1.14 WHIP and a .226 opponent batting average in 56 starts, and finishing his 2023 All-Star season as the runner-up to New York-AL’s Gerrit Cole for the AL Cy Young Award.
 The three-time All-Star ranks fourth among all active pitchers in starts (359) and wins (143); fifth in quality starts (193); sixth in innings pitched (2087.0), ERA (3.51), opponent OPS (.662) and strikeouts (2,074); and eighth in opponent batting average (.233) and WHIP (1.19). Over the last three seasons he ranks ninth in baseball in strikeouts (553), recording 200-plus strikeouts in two of those three seasons.
 The Smyrna, Tennessee native has pitched in parts of 14 major league seasons with the Oakland Athletics (2013-17), New York Yankees (2017-18), Cincinnati Reds (2019-21), Twins (2022-23), St. Louis Cardinals (2024-25) and Red Sox (2026). Over his career, he has posted a record of 143-107 with a 3.51 ERA (2087.0 IP, 814 ER), 193 quality starts, 667 walks, 2074 strikeouts, a 1.19 WHIP and a .233 opponent batting average in 368 games (359 starts).
